restoration_note: Teaching describes the three Rocks (ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲁ) — confirmed truths in ultimates — set by the Greatness in the outer worlds: the Pillar of Glory / Perfect Man (bearing-up), the new Land of Light upon the Land of Darkness (subduing), and the great Thought / Jesus the Radiance (awakening Call). All sixteen gaps are short editorial restorations tightly constrained by Lycopolitan grammar (article Ⲧ- on ordinal feminines, prefix ⲁϥ-, possessive ⲛⲉϩ-, agent ϩⲓⲧⲙ̄ ⲡ-, completion of ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ across the line break, idiom ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲟⲩ split across the column) and by the lexicon's fixed term ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ for the Pillar of Glory. Nothing in the core was too damaged to restore.

restorations.basis: Standard completion of ⲛⲓⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'the worlds'; only -ⲟⲥ is lost. Two characters, fixed by the Greek loanword.

Lexicon entry: Pillar of Glory = ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ = ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧⲭⲏⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('Perfect Man'). The whole-teaching reading identifies the first rock as the bearing-up Pillar / Omophoros that lifts the cosmos upward.
Completion of ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲩⲧⲁϩⲙⲉϥ 'whom they summoned-him' (idiom ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ); cf. parallel ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲩⲧⲁϩⲙⲉϥ in 3814.
Agent marker ϩⲓⲧⲙ̄ ⲡ- before ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ — standard syntax for the agent of ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. The Ambassador (lexicon: Third Ambassador) is the calling agent.
est_chars=2; 3sg.m. perfective prefix ⲁϥ- governing ⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. for ϫⲡⲟ 'set/establish'), parallel to the chain of ⲁϥ-verbs that follows (ⲁϥⲃⲓ, ⲁϥϣⲱⲡⲉ, ⲁϥⲥⲉϩⲟ, ⲁϥⲧⲁⲭⲣⲟ).
Editor's prefix completion (apparently double-marked with {4}); 3sg.m. perfective ⲁϥ- on ⲭⲡⲟ.
Line-break completion of ⲡⲕⲟⲥ|ⲙⲟⲥ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'the entire cosmos'; the ⲧ is the start of ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄.
Lyc. possessive ⲛⲉϩ- 'his' on plural ϩⲃⲁⲙ (pl. of ϭⲟⲙ 'power'); reads ⲛⲉϩⲃⲁⲙ 'his powers'.
Single-letter completion of ϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'works' (pl. of ϩⲱⲃ); the heavenly states established for those above and below are 'the works' the Pillar fixes.
Feminine article Ⲧ- on the ordinal Ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛ̄ⲧⲉ 'the second' (agreeing with feminine ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲁ as ordinal-fem.).
Feminine article Ⲧ- on the ordinal Ⲧⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ 'the third'; parallel to {9}.
Demonstrative Ⲛⲉⲓ̈ ⲛⲉ 'these are' opening the summary clause that gathers the three rocks; standard Lyc. summative formula.
Trace of ⲉ visible; ⲓ restored to complete ⲁⲩⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they came forth' (ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ idiom of emanation/issuing).
Genitive linker ⲛ- between ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲃ ('a great') and ⲕⲁϩⲧⲏϥ ('trust/confidence'): 'a great trust' — the single inmost intention from which the three rocks issue.
First half of split ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'they alone / by themselves'; line-end fragment continued at start of next column.
Second half of split ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲟⲩ; combines with preceding {14} ⲟⲩ + following ⲉⲧⲟⲩ (visible) to yield ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲧⲟⲩ.
